problem: Current VLN agents barely use visual information: R2R instructions are high-level and written for expert (human) navigators, so models overfit to text and generalize poorly to unseen environments. Speaker-generated augmentation instructions are also low quality (wrong orientation, missing relevant content).
motivation: Blinding the visual features of Self-Monitoring and Regretful-Agent costs only a few SR points in unseen environments, which suggests the agents rely on textual and dataset biases rather than on vision. The authors therefore target the training data, aiming for instructions that reference visible objects so that vision becomes necessary.
key_idea: Train the Speaker with two auxiliary losses built from Matterport3D object metadata (recommended object words and rule-based crafted instructions), so that generated augmentation instructions are semantically richer and more visually grounded, then use them for agent pre-training.
insight: Blind ablations show a large drop in seen environments (SR about 60% to about 30%) but only a few points in unseen ones (Regretful-Agent 0.43 vs 0.36 blind), which indicates memorization rather than visual grounding. Removing all text still gives 25% SR, showing a strong dataset bias. Object-grounded Speaker instructions give about twice the pre-training gain of the base Speaker for Regretful-Agent (0.43 to 0.51 vs 0.47). Purely rule-based crafted instructions reach 0.46 without any human text, and the base Speaker's gain seems to come from quantity (178k routes) rather than quality.
method: Speaker base: Speaker-Follower speaker, an encoder over panoramic views and actions plus an LSTM decoder, generates instructions for 178,300 sampled paths, with NLL against the 3 human instructions.
360-visualization tool: scripts over Matterport3DMeta that fetch objects (position, size, distance, heading, elevation) and navigable viewpoints for each node.

Crafted instructions: for each node, a rule-based atomic instruction picks the best nearby object relative to the next node (e.g. 'Turn left, walk straight down the left of the painting'), and the atomic instructions are concatenated per path.

Objects auxiliary task: objects are filtered by distance, area, uniqueness and usability; the top N per node are assigned to instruction words by index, and an extra NLL term weighted by lambda pushes the speaker to emit those objects.
Crafted auxiliary task: word-by-word NLL against the crafted instruction, weighted by beta, is added to the speaker loss.
Two-phase agent training: Phase I pre-trains the navigator (Regretful-Agent, and HAMT) on generated or crafted instructions, and Phase II fine-tunes on the original human data.

setting.backbone: Regretful-Agent (ResNet-152 features) and HAMT as navigators; Speaker-Follower speaker (LSTM) trained with auxiliary losses to generate instructions
setting.training_data: R2R train (4675 human instructions in the train set) plus 178,300 speaker-generated or crafted synthetic instructions for pre-training; Matterport3DMeta object labels
setting.privileged: Matterport3D object metadata (GT object labels/positions) used during training-data generation only, not at test time

numbers_note: Only the val seen/unseen splits are reported; no test-server numbers for the proposed method. Table 1 lists other methods on the test set. Metrics for Regretful-Agent are printed as fractions (0.51) and copied as printed.
results: With the object auxiliary task, Regretful-Agent unseen SR rises from 0.43 (no pre-training) to 0.51, versus 0.47 with the base Speaker. On HAMT, SR goes from 48.7 to about 52.4-52.6, against 52.3 for the base Speaker, so the extra gain is small.
limitations: Depends on Matterport3D object metadata, so it does not transfer to new environments without an object detector.

The gain on HAMT over the base Speaker is marginal, only Regretful-Agent and HAMT were tested, and the results are single runs with no variance reported. The 'reliance on text' claim is supported only by blind-vision experiments on older models.
